lever: jsonesc: one line appended to the Rules of prompts/system.md: tool replies are JSON, so file text inside them is escaped (one backslash shows as \\, a double quote as \", a line break as \n); in edits and scripts write the file's real characters; if an old block is not found, check this first.
why: Mechanism: swegemma 0.2.11 + ADK send tool results JSON-encoded once (code, pinned by a test; host-confirmed for the scorer since the 09-30 wheelhouse), so rich/ansi.py's raw regex \x1b reaches the model as \\x1b. Four box runs (p4, p4_v7, p4_v7c, p4_v7d) wrote that reply form into the file: 0 of 16 hidden tests, 6 existing ones broken, then 37-42 identical no-op resends. p4_b1024 (v13's prompt line) re-typed the regex in the doubled form in 5 of its 9 experiments (93-228 s), never edited, and hit the cap. Measured through v13's own edit template on the base snapshot (scripts/forty_two/rich_solve/ev_jsonesc.py): old and new copied from the reply -> refused (AssertionError 0); real characters -> 23 of 23 pass with the hidden tests; real old + reply-form new -> 22 failed (the box failure). v13 also removed the safety net: it dropped edit_file, whose unescape fallback rescued 21 of 95 successful p4_b1024 edits in 10 tasks. Evidence: docs/forty_two/evidence/rich_solve_jsonesc.txt. Applies outside the 42: rich_3063 ('Fix escaping trailing backslash', solved by other runs, failed by p4_b1024 after 7 python experiments on backslash reprs); 13 of the 14 public tasks whose gold changes a line with a backslash are in the 42 (P = 0.0019 if unrelated), and 166 of 1,044 held-out tasks change such a line.
alternative: submissions/v13_modtests (commit 520358f5): p4_v0t2 wrote the backslashes right and passed all 16 hidden tests, but its character class swallowed '[' and broke 3 existing tests in tests/test_ansi.py, which a 0.1 s run of that file shows (docs/forty_two/evidence/rich_solve_modtests.txt). Queue it here if v13_jsonesc samples write correct escapes and still break test_decode.
expected: maybe: the lever removes the escaping failure of 5 of 6 runs; the character-class semantics still have to be right (v0-think's error)
baseline: p4 (v5h2), p4_v7, p4_v7c, p4_v7d, p4_b1024 (v12-b1024), p4_v0t2 (v0-think) all failed; 2 of 12 Kaggle L4 runs solved
regression_risk: 75 tokens on every call (about 9 % more system prompt; under 2 % of a typical 5-14k-token request). The rule is the exact decoding of the reply format, so a correct reading is unchanged; the risk is a model that over-applies it and halves backslashes that really are doubled in the file (a Python non-raw string holding a literal backslash). No solved task is known to depend on writing an escaped form; the solved tasks whose p4_b1024 edits needed the unescape fallback (fastapi_14077, fastapi_14301, fastapi_5077; p4_v0t2: fastapi_13537, fastapi_14463, fastapi_14794, rich_2943, rich_3454) are the ones v13 exposes to exact matching, and this line is aimed at helping them. Inferred, not measured.
box_risk: Text-call leaks are not new (coordinator: 10 leaked replies over the six earlier box runs, all recovered after the nudge); new on the v13 screen is one first-reply leak that never recovered (fastapi_14487), cause undecided, v13 not treated as broken. This bundle inherits v13's fenced heredoc in step 3 unchanged; the added line has no fenced block, backtick, brace or tool-call-shaped text (pinned by tests/test_v13_rich_solve.py). A sample with 0 tool calls points at the base, not at this lever.
